title: Grade 4 SOCIAL STUDIES — Premium Revision Paper #11

pages.quiz:
SOCIAL STUDIES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #11
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these is a cardinal point? (1 mark)
   A. South-west
   B. North-east
   C. West
   D. North-west

2. In the morning, your shadow falls towards which direction? (1 mark)
   A. The sun
   B. Nowhere
   C. East
   D. West

3. What does a map key explain? (1 mark)
   A. The name of the map maker
   B. The meaning of the colours and symbols
   C. The weather
   D. The date of the map

4. A county is divided into smaller parts called what? (1 mark)
   A. Sub-counties
   B. Continents
   C. Oceans
   D. Countries

5. Which is the largest county in Kenya by area? (1 mark)
   A. Turkana
   B. Kisumu
   C. Nairobi
   D. Mombasa

6. On a physical map, what colour is used for water? (1 mark)
   A. Black
   B. Blue
   C. Brown
   D. Red

7. What is a valley? (1 mark)
   A. A very high peak
   B. A big lake
   C. A huge flat plain
   D. Low land between hills or mountains

8. Which physical feature is best for building roads, towns and farms easily? (1 mark)
   A. A steep mountain
   B. A deep valley
   C. A plain
   D. A waterfall

9. Why are mountains important for water? (1 mark)
   A. They catch rain and give rise to rivers
   B. They make the land flat
   C. They dry up lakes
   D. They stop all rain

10. What is the difference between a museum and a cultural centre? (1 mark)
   A. A cultural centre has no dances
   B. A museum is always outdoors
   C. There is no difference
   D. A museum mainly keeps objects, a cultural centre shows living culture

11. Which of these is a service learning activity at a historic site? (1 mark)
   A. Painting graffiti
   B. Building a fire
   C. Sweeping and collecting litter
   D. Selling tickets to friends

12. What is a museum? (1 mark)
   A. A bus stage
   B. A kind of factory
   C. A building where old objects are kept and shown
   D. A place where crops are grown

13. What is a historic built environment? (1 mark)
   A. A natural forest
   B. A place built long ago that tells us about the past
   C. A new shopping mall
   D. A river

14. Why do herders in dry areas not live crowded in one place? (1 mark)
   A. They have no families
   B. They do not use water
   C. They dislike roads
   D. They move with animals to look for water and grass

15. Which is a reason why fewer people live in a forest reserve? (1 mark)
   A. It has many towns
   B. There are too many houses
   C. People are not allowed to settle there
   D. It has good roads

16. Which of these is an artefact? (1 mark)
   A. A river
   B. A clay pot
   C. A mountain
   D. A cloud

17. Which of these is a traditional drink of the Kalenjin? (1 mark)
   A. Mursik
   B. Wine
   C. Cola
   D. Coffee

18. Which is a good manner when interviewing an elder about culture? (1 mark)
   A. Refusing to listen
   B. Laughing
   C. Greeting politely and asking permission to record
   D. Interrupting

19. Which practice do Kenyan laws forbid because it harms girls? (1 mark)
   A. Cooking ugali
   B. Wearing beads
   C. Female genital mutilation
   D. Playing bao

20. Which resource gives electric power from underground steam at Olkaria? (1 mark)
   A. Coal
   B. Oil
   C. Geothermal heat
   D. Wind

21. Which town is Kenya's main port and a busy industrial town? (1 mark)
   A. Kitui
   B. Nyeri
   C. Mombasa
   D. Kericho

22. What is one way factories can protect the environment? (1 mark)
   A. Throw waste into rivers
   B. Burn tyres
   C. Treat waste before releasing it
   D. Cut all trees

23. Who should handle sharp tools in a school project? (1 mark)
   A. A visitor
   B. An adult
   C. A young child alone
   D. Nobody

24. Which of these is a quality of a good citizen in school? (1 mark)
   A. Bullying
   B. Laziness
   C. Cheating
   D. Honesty

25. If you see a pupil being bullied, what should you do? (1 mark)
   A. Laugh
   B. Join in
   C. Ignore
   D. Tell a trusted adult and support the pupil

26. Which of these is a way of living in peace with others? (1 mark)
   A. Grabbing things
   B. Cheating
   C. Teasing
   D. Sharing what you have

27. Which activity builds peace in school? (1 mark)
   A. A fight
   B. A peace poster competition
   C. Spreading rumours
   D. Cheating

28. What should you do if someone makes you feel unsafe? (1 mark)
   A. Fight
   B. Keep it a secret
   C. Say no, go to a safe place and tell a trusted adult
   D. Stay silent

29. Why is early marriage harmful? (1 mark)
   A. It stops education and harms health
   B. It helps children learn
   C. It is fun
   D. It makes children rich

30. Which action helps a child with special needs? (1 mark)
   A. Laughing at them
   B. Including them in games
   C. Neglecting them
   D. Hiding them

31. What is an election? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of game
   B. A process where people vote to choose leaders
   C. A school holiday
   D. A prayer

32. In a mock session, what should pupils do first after opening? (1 mark)
   A. Read the last minutes
   B. Leave
   C. Close the meeting
   D. Fight

33. Which item usually comes last on an agenda? (1 mark)
   A. Closing remarks
   B. Reading of minutes
   C. Opening prayer
   D. Reports

34. Who leads the meetings of the assembly of pupils? (1 mark)
   A. The Speaker
   B. The driver
   C. The gatekeeper
   D. The cook

35. What is a Children's Government in school? (1 mark)
   A. A group of parents
   B. A group of teachers
   C. The government of Kenya
   D. A group of elected pupils who help to run the school

36. Which minister would organise a football match between classes? (1 mark)
   A. Health
   B. Library
   C. Environment
   D. Sports and games

37. Who is a leader? (1 mark)
   A. A person who guides and helps others to do something good
   B. A machine
   C. A person who breaks rules
   D. A stranger

38. Which quality means not boasting or looking down on others? (1 mark)
   A. Humility
   B. Pride
   C. Greed
   D. Anger

39. What are ECDE and pre-primary schools run by? (1 mark)
   A. Private banks only
   B. The army
   C. Foreign governments
   D. County governments

40. What does the county assembly do? (1 mark)
   A. Trains footballers
   B. Cooks meals
   C. Makes county laws and approves the budget
   D. Drives buses

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Give two responsibilities of a child at school. (2 marks)

42. Give two reasons why some areas are densely populated. (2 marks)

43. State three causes of child abuse in a community. (3 marks)

44. Name four roles in a school enterprise team and state one duty for each. (4 marks)

45. A group spent Ksh 900 and earned Ksh 600. Say whether this is a profit or a loss and find the amount. Suggest two reasons why it may have happened. (4 marks)

46. State three industries found in Kenya and the raw material each uses. (3 marks)

47. Give two reasons why some areas are sparsely populated. (2 marks)

48. Explain the difference between the governor and the president. (3 marks)

49. State three functions of the Children's Government. (3 marks)

50. Explain what a raw material is and give one example. (2 marks)

51. Describe how to stay safe during a visit to a factory. Give four rules. (4 marks)

52. Describe four things a school can do to promote child rights. (4 marks)

53. Give three things that should be on a sketch map of your county. (3 marks)

54. On a sketch map the school is in the middle, the market is above it and the clinic is below it. Write two sentences to say where the market and the clinic are. (4 marks)

55. Explain what an industry is. (2 marks)

56. Describe five actions that show good citizenship in school. (5 marks)

57. Describe how a pupil can help a new pupil to settle in. (3 marks)

58. State three things that spoil peace in school. (3 marks)

59. Explain how good citizenship in school prepares pupils to be good citizens of Kenya. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #11 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — West
   Only north, east, south and west are cardinal points. The others are in-between points.

2. D — West
   The sun is in the east in the morning, so shadows point west.

3. B — The meaning of the colours and symbols
   The key tells what each line, colour and symbol stands for.

4. A — Sub-counties
   Counties are divided into sub-counties, and sub-counties into wards.

5. A — Turkana
   Turkana is the largest county by land area.

6. B — Blue
   Blue is used for lakes, rivers and the ocean.

7. D — Low land between hills or mountains
   A valley is a low area between higher land.

8. C — A plain
   Flat land is easy to build on and farm.

9. A — They catch rain and give rise to rivers
   Mountains catch rain and feed rivers.

10. D — A museum mainly keeps objects, a cultural centre shows living culture
   Cultural centres let visitors see and take part in living culture.

11. C — Sweeping and collecting litter
   Cleaning up is a way of serving and conserving.

12. C — A building where old objects are kept and shown
   Museums keep artefacts safely and show them to people.

13. B — A place built long ago that tells us about the past
   Historic built places are old places made by people.

14. D — They move with animals to look for water and grass
   Herding needs large areas of pasture.

15. C — People are not allowed to settle there
   Forest reserves are protected.

16. B — A clay pot
   A clay pot is made by people.

17. A — Mursik
   Mursik is fermented milk.

18. C — Greeting politely and asking permission to record
   Politeness shows respect.

19. C — Female genital mutilation
   FGM is against the law.

20. C — Geothermal heat
   Olkaria makes electricity from geothermal steam.

21. C — Mombasa
   Mombasa is Kenya's main port.

22. C — Treat waste before releasing it
   Treating waste avoids pollution.

23. B — An adult
   Adults must handle dangerous tools.

24. D — Honesty
   Honesty is a positive quality.

25. D — Tell a trusted adult and support the pupil
   Reporting helps to stop bullying.

26. D — Sharing what you have
   Sharing shows kindness.

27. B — A peace poster competition
   Competitions on peace teach and encourage it.

28. C — Say no, go to a safe place and tell a trusted adult
   Telling an adult is right.

29. A — It stops education and harms health
   Early marriage harms girls and boys.

30. B — Including them in games
   Children with special needs have equal rights.

31. B — A process where people vote to choose leaders
   Elections choose leaders.

32. A — Read the last minutes
   Minutes remind the group of past decisions.

33. A — Closing remarks
   Meetings end with closing remarks.

34. A — The Speaker
   The Speaker leads meetings.

35. D — A group of elected pupils who help to run the school
   It is made up of pupils chosen by their classmates.

36. D — Sports and games
   Sports leaders organise games.

37. A — A person who guides and helps others to do something good
   Leaders guide and help.

38. A — Humility
   Humble leaders are modest.

39. D — County governments
   Pre-primary education is a county function.

40. C — Makes county laws and approves the budget
   The assembly makes laws and approves the budget.

SECTION B
----
41. (2 marks)
   Answer: Attend and study hard, and respect others. Accept care for property.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each responsibility.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: Good rain and fertile soil for farming, and jobs and services in towns. Accept water or good roads.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Poverty, harmful beliefs and lack of knowledge of the law. Accept greed or conflict.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each cause.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: Project manager leads the team, treasurer keeps money records, production team makes the goods, sales team sells the goods.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each role and duty pair.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: It is a loss of Ksh 300. Sales may have been low because the price was too high or not enough people knew about the goods.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for loss, 1 mark for the amount 900 - 600 = 300, 1 mark for each reason.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: Sugar factory uses sugarcane, tea factory uses tea leaves, cement factory uses limestone.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each industry with its material.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: Very little rain and no water, and thick forests, swamps or steep land. Accept game parks or few roads.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: The president leads the national government of the whole country. The governor leads one county government.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each description and 1 mark for the difference.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: Represent pupils, help keep order, and promote cleanliness. Accept organising activities.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each function.

50. (2 marks)
   Answer: A raw material is a material used to make something new, for example sugarcane used to make sugar.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meaning, 1 mark for example.

51. (4 marks)
   Answer: Stay with the group, do not touch machines, listen to the guide, and wear safety clothing if given.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

52. (4 marks)
   Answer: Make posters, sing songs on child protection, set up a suggestion box, and include all children in activities.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each activity.

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: A title, a north arrow and a key. Accept sub-county names and boundaries.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct item.

54. (4 marks)
   Answer: The market is north of the school. The clinic is south of the school.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct direction word and 1 mark for each correct sentence.

55. (2 marks)
   Answer: An industry is a place or business where raw materials are made into goods, or where a service is given to many people.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for making goods, 1 mark for services or raw materials.

56. (5 marks)
   Answer: Arrive on time, keep the compound clean, respect teachers, share with others, and report bullying.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each action.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: Welcome the pupil, show the classrooms and toilets, and invite the pupil to play.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: Bullying, fighting and spreading rumours. Accept stealing or discrimination.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

59. (4 marks)
   Answer: Pupils learn to follow rules, respect others, take care of public property and take responsibility. These habits continue when they are adults.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.
